claim: Supabase Free tier projects are paused after 1 week (7 days) of inactivity, the single biggest gotcha for a non-technical participant returning weeks later.
quote: Free projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity. Limit of 2 active projects.

claim: The Supabase pause-on-inactivity problem is well-known enough that community keep-alive tools (GitHub Actions cron pingers) exist specifically to work around it.
quote: Prevent Supabase projects from getting paused due to inactivity

claim: Vercel Hobby has no inactivity-based suspension; deployments persist indefinitely and retention is unlimited by default, but the plan is officially restricted to non-commercial personal use.
quote: As stated in the fair use guidelines, the Hobby plan restricts users to non-commercial, personal use only. ... Deployment Retention: Unlimited by default.

claim: On Render's free tier, web services spin down after 15 minutes of inactivity and take roughly one minute to restart on the next request.
quote: Free web services spin down after 15 minutes of inactivity and restart on the next request, with spin-up taking about one minute.

claim: The Render cold-start UX failure is exactly the 'show grandma' problem: visitors see a dead-looking screen for 30-50 seconds and assume the app is broken.
quote: You send a recruiter, client, or investor a link to your project and the first thing they experience is a dead-looking screen. ... For 30, 40, sometimes 50 seconds. ... Most people won't wait. They'll assume it's broken and move on.

claim: Render's free PostgreSQL databases now expire 30 days after creation (cut from 90), with a 14-day grace period before deletion and no backups available - a guaranteed data-loss event for any workshop participant who needed a DB.
quote: newly created Free Render PostgreSQL databases expire after 30 days (previously 90)... After a Free database expires, you have a grace period of 14 days to upgrade it to a paid instance type. After the grace period, Render deletes the database (along with all of its data).

claim: Replit free-tier apps sleep after about 5 minutes of inactivity with a 10-30 second cold start, and always-on requires Replit Core at $20/month or higher.
quote: your Replit app goes to sleep after approximately 5 minutes of inactivity. ... cold starts take 10 to 30 seconds depending on your app's size and dependencies. ... For anything customer-facing... 30 seconds of downtime on every visit is a dealbreaker.

claim: Railway has no permanent free tier - it offers only a 30-day trial with $5 credit and a credit card required at signup, after which services are paused until upgrade to Hobby ($5/mo) or Pro ($20/mo).
quote: Railway offers a 30-day free trial with $5 in credits... After your $5 trial credits are used up or 30 days pass (whichever comes first), your services are paused. You'll need to upgrade to Hobby ($5/mo) or Pro ($20/mo) to continue.

claim: Fly.io no longer has a free tier for new signups in 2026; only a 2-VM-hour or 7-day trial, after which a credit card and pay-as-you-go are required.
quote: Fly.io does not have a free tier in 2026. New users get a free trial limited to 2 VM hours or 7 days (whichever ends first). Fly.io removed free allowances for new customers in 2024.

claim: Cloudflare Workers/Pages free tier gives 100,000 requests/day with no cold starts (V8 isolates start in under 5ms) and Cloudflare Pages has no bandwidth limit at any tier - structurally immune to the sleep/cold-start grandma problem.
quote: Cloudflare Workers don't use containers but instead use V8 Isolates... which can start in under 5 milliseconds—eliminating cold starts effectively. ... The free plan includes 100,000 requests per day

claim: Neon Postgres free tier always scales to zero after 5 minutes of inactivity, but resumes within a few hundred milliseconds - effectively transparent to visitors, unlike Supabase's 30-second wake-from-pause.
quote: On the Free plan, scale to zero is always enabled and automatically suspends your compute after 5 minutes of inactivity. ... Once you query the database again, it reactivates automatically within a few hundred milliseconds.

claim: PlanetScale removed its free Hobby tier in April 2024; cheapest entry is $5/month, ruling it out for a take-home workshop deployment.
quote: PlanetScale eliminated its free Hobby tier in April 2024, with the cheapest entry point now being $5/month

claim: Turso's free tier is always-on with no pause-on-inactivity (9 GB storage), making it one of the few DB choices that survives months of dormancy without ceremony.
quote: Turso's free tier includes 9 GB of storage and is always-on, meaning databases do not pause due to inactivity.

claim: Netlify free plan does not suspend for inactivity, only for exceeding the 100 GB bandwidth / 300 build minutes / 125k function invocations quota - in which case all sites pause until the next month with no auto-recharge.
quote: Free gives you 300 credits per month with a hard limit, no auto-recharge, and no overage. ... If your app or site exceeds the Free plan limits for the month, it will be suspended for the remaining days in the calendar month.

claim: Lovable's free tier is permanent (5 daily credits, public projects, lovable.app subdomain) but cloud-backed projects pause when the $25/month free cloud credits are exhausted, which is a separate inactivity-independent failure mode.
quote: Lovable.dev's free tier is free forever for 5 daily credits and public projects only. ... when cloud credits are exhausted, projects pause until you add funds or enable auto-top-up.
